title: rate-engine-epoch-rollback-causing-silent-overdrafts
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Intermittent silent overdrafts observed after shard reassignments and epoch reconciliations. Tokens are allowed past configured per-key/per-route burst windows without generating throttles or billing events for a short period (tens of seconds). This ticket captures investigation, repro, root cause analysis, and a rollout plan for a fix.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Ava Martinez: Initial report from payments: two customers saw brief token usage spikes that did not appear in billing events or throttle logs for ~25s after a scheduled shard reassignment. Affects per-org burst credits and per-route short-window policies. Raising P1 due to potential underbilling and customer-visible limit slip-through.

2026-03-01 - Ravi Patel: Reproduced locally using unit test harness that simulates shard handoff. Observed that after finishing an epoch compaction step during reassignment, the in-memory token buckets on the target shard were initialized from a compacted snapshot that occasionally omitted recently-applied debits (race between compacter and inflight apply path). Result: bucket balance briefly higher than authoritative ledger, allowing overdraft.

2026-03-02 - Ravi Patel: Reproduction steps: 1) Run two shards with split keyspace 2) Create steady traffic against route A to accrue near-zero burst 3) Trigger shard move with concurrent 200 rps spike 4) Observe traffic allowed beyond configured burst for ~10-40s on target shard. Logs attached: /logs/rateengine/overdraft-2026-03-02.log.

2026-03-04 - Mariya Kovalenko (PM): Customer impact: medium-high. Some customers bypassed short-window per-route throttles; billing records later reconciled but cause delayed invoices and anomalies in usage dashboards. Need a short-term mitigation and long-term correctness fix.

2026-03-05 - Ravi Patel: Root cause hypothesis: during compaction/epoch-rollback path we apply a snapshot that contains monotonic counters up to N, but our local in-flight debit buffer (delta since last snapshot) can be lost if compactor wins the race and we then roll back and reapply in a different order. The consequence is an effective negative delta not persisted, so target shard assumes less consumption. Observed in codepath: rateengine/storage/snapshot_compactor.go and rateengine/engine/apply.go.

2026-03-06 - Engineering note: Candidate fixes evaluated: (A) Make compactor atomic wrt inflight delta flush (B) Persist inflight deltas to a temporary WAL before compaction (C) Change reconciliation to use authoritative ledger fetch from global metastore during handoff. Tradeoffs: A minimal but risky around locking; B increases write-amplification; C adds RPC latency during reassignment but is simpler correctness-wise.

2026-03-07 - Decision: Implement C for hotfix (fetch authoritative ledger on handoff) and follow-up with B as durable prevention. Will implement C as change in shard-handshake: target shard will query metastore for last_applied_seq and ledger_deltas and reconcile before accepting traffic.

2026-03-08 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/4312 implementing authoritative-ledger-fetch-on-handoff. Includes unit tests that simulate inflight apply races and one integration test with real shard handoff via docker-compose.

2026-03-09 - Code review feedback from Jessica Li: Please add a metric for 'handoff_reconcile_discrepancy_count' and a gauge for 'reconciled_delta_bytes' to track how often the ledger diverges between source and target. Also add a safety cap to avoid negative bucket resets (never lower local observed consumption).

2026-03-10 - Ravi Patel: Added metrics and safety cap in PR. Ran end-to-end test harness for 50 handoffs under load; no overdrafts observed. Logs: /artifacts/handoff-tests/2026-03-10/results.txt. Noted a 6-12ms median latency increase on handoff path which is acceptable for correctness.

2026-03-11 - QA: Running canary against staging with genuine traffic shape for 48h, instrumented dashboards at https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ratelimit/handoff-reconcile showing zero incidents in canary group. Also validated billing pipeline reconciles properly.

2026-03-12 - Deployment plan: 1) Merge PR to release branch after final +2 approval 2) Deploy runtime-1.20-hotfix to dedicated canary pool (node pool tag: canary-ratelimit-0312) 3) Monitor 'handoff_reconcile_discrepancy_count' and per-org throttle misses for 2h 4) Gradual rollout to all regions over 6h 5) Postmortem and follow-up ticket to implement durable WAL deltas (B). Owners: Ravi + SRE (Kofi Mensah).

2026-03-12 - Follow-ups: Create ENG-142209 to track WAL-based durable deltas and chaos tests for shard splits; create PM ticket to inform billing/finance of expected short-term invoice reconcilations.
